Take -5 to hit for +10 damage — the biggest damage line a ranger can take, and Archery style (lvl 2, +2 to hit) buys back most of the penalty. Everything else on a ranged ranger is commentary on this feat.
Bonus-action hand-crossbow shot plus no disadvantage in melee — a third -5/+10 attack every round once Sharpshooter is online. The two feats are one build.

The power subclass. Turn one: an extra attack, +10 ft move, +1d8 on the bonus hit. Umbral Sight makes you invisible to darkvision — and in Hell EVERYTHING has darkvision. You are a ghost on the one plane built entirely on seeing in the dark.

The nova opener: surprise gives assassin autocrits, Dread Ambusher gives the extra first-turn attack, Sharpshooter stacks -5/+10 on every swing. Round one deletes a lieutenant before initiative settles.

The charmer chassis: +1d4 psychic on weapon hits, Wisdom feeds your face skills, free charm person by lvl 5. Mechanically solid and it is literally a snake charmer — the Cha-keyed tricks ride on the yuan-ti +2 Cha.
A swarm that follows you and eats people — reflavor it as SNAKES and the theme writes itself. Per hit: +1d6 damage, or shove them 15 ft, or teleport yourself 5 ft. Level 8 adds flight.

The fiend-hunter's fiend-hunter: +1d8 force damage, portal senses, banishing smite at 9 — it sends things back to their home plane. You are already on their home plane. It was written for this campaign.

Primal Companion — reflavor Beast of the Land as a giant constrictor and Acosta becomes a real stat block: HP scales with you, acts on your command as a bonus action, revives with a spell slot. The old PHB beast master is why the ranger had a bad rep; the TCE one is good.

Magical darkness beats normal darkvision — even fiends cannot see through it. Devil's Sight (warlock 2) can. You attack with advantage; they swing blind. In a plane where darkness is the weather, this is a siege engine.
Do not want the warlock dip? One feat buys Devil's Sight outright — same darkness combo, zero multiclass levels. Pick it at any ASI.
One level: your attack stat becomes Cha (which yuan-ti already boosts), plus Hexblade's Curse for +prof damage on a chosen target. Turns a skill monkey into a duelist on the stat he already has.

Expertise x2 — double Stealth or Deception so the criminal resume is mechanically literal — plus Sneak Attack dice on a Sharpshooter shot. Rogue 2 adds Cunning Action: dash, disengage, or hide as a bonus action every turn.

The TCE fix for Favored Enemy: mark a target for +1d4 damage per hit (d6 at 6, d8 at 14), free, no slot, but it eats concentration — meaning it competes with Hunter's Mark, not complements it. Pick one.
The best 1st-level damage button a ranger owns: bonus action, advantage on one hit, +1d8, and you stop provoking opportunity attacks. Use it to land the Sharpshooter shot that matters.
+1d6 on every hit against the mark — Sharpshooter hits included — for an hour, movable between kills. The real cost is concentration: do not double-book it with another concentration trick.
+10 to the whole party's stealth for an hour — the infiltration button. Criminal background written in spell slots: everyone walks in, nobody hears a thing.
Reaction: halve fire/acid/etc damage and add 1d6 of that element to your next hit. In Avernus everything breathes fire; yuan-ti already has poison covered — this covers the plane's actual weather.
One slot, up to eight poisonous snakes under your command — the snake charmer's graduation exam. Also just objectively the strongest 3rd-level summon in the game.
Reach weapon plus a d4 butt-strike as a bonus action, and things that enter your reach eat a reaction attack. The melee counterpart of the Crossbow Expert play.
The lockdown pair: stop-on-hit (Sentinel) triggers off the reach attack (PAM), so things that walk up to you freeze in place at 10 ft out. Turns a melee build into area denial.
Rangers fail Wisdom saves constantly and there is no class feature covering it. +1 Wis and save proficiency patches the biggest hole in the chassis.
+5 initiative and immune to surprise — stacks with Gloom Stalker's ambush math. In Hell, where everything ambushes, going first is a build feature.
After every rest: temp HP for the whole party equal to level+Cha. The yuan-ti +2 Cha makes it land, and a snake charmer rallying a room is on-brand.
+1 Cha, mimic voices perfectly, advantage on Deception when impersonating someone. It is literally the Epstein skillset printed as a feat. Criminal synergy is self-evident.
Three free rerolls a day, yours or theirs. Narratively accurate — his whole existence is luck running out, and now it's a resource you manage.
Eldritch blast for a real ranged option plus Hex once a day — a warlock dip with no multiclass level spent. Pairs with the yuan-ti Cha.
Half-elves and elves only: when you have advantage on a Dex attack, reroll one die — triple-advantage. Sharpshooter crit-fishing goes from good to absurd.
Small races only: +1 Str or Dex, extra speed, advantage to escape grapples — turns a halfling into a slippery skirmisher.
Humans, half-elves, half-orcs: +1 skill, +1 tool, and one expertise. Cheap, quiet, and the single most efficient skill-monkey feat.
Dwarves only: spend a hit die as a bonus action to heal. Your hit dice become a combat resource instead of a rest resource.

The assassin-bruiser classic: Reckless Attack gives YOURSELF advantage on Str attacks — finesse weapons still count — so Sneak Attack fires every turn with no flanking and no setup. Barb 5 for Extra Attack and Bear Totem 3 resists everything coming back. Rage is just gravy.

Smite spends any slot, and sorcerer levels pile up slots — plus Quickened Spell means spell AND full smite-attack routine in the same turn. The dedicated nova machine: one boss round, triple-digit damage, everyone at the table goes quiet.
One hexblade level: attacks run on Cha (drop Str entirely), and pact slots recharge on a SHORT rest — your smite economy refills at lunch. Widely considered the strongest paladin chassis in 2014.
The gish that loses nothing: Cha to attacks, medium armor and shield proficiency from the dip, full bard casting underneath, flourishes on top. All the swordplay, none of the stat split.

Pact slots convert to sorcery points, pact magic recharges on short rest — with enough short rests the loop has no ceiling. The famous infinite-slot exploit. Most DMs cap it; everyone knows it; nobody's proud. Knowing it exists is the point.

Wild shape into a 34-HP bear, rage inside the bear — resistance to nearly everything on top of a disposable HP pool that resets per short rest. The cheapest tank math in the game: you ARE the hit points.

Two levels of fighter in anything: a whole extra action once per rest. On a caster that's two fireballs in one turn; on a martial it's the whole attack routine twice. The most stapled-on dip in the game.

One cleric level grants heavy armor and shields on a full caster — wizard in plate, hit points keep pace with level, and Life/Nature/Tempest each add a real feature. One level slows your spell table by exactly one level.
Bond allies get +1d4 to attacks, checks, AND saves between each other, reaction-free — and it STACKS with bless. Arguably the strongest single level printed in 2014; a lot of tables ban it outright.

Aura of Conquest drops feared creatures to zero movement; wrathful smite or an undead/GOO warlock applies the fear. Frightened AND speed 0 AND they can't approach — the lockdown loop: they can't move, can't fight, can't leave.

Channel: the target's next hit takes DOUBLE damage — vulnerability on command. Feed it to a paladin's smite crit or an assassin's autocrit and a boss loses half its health bar to a single swing. The support pick that makes novas nuclear.
Two d20s rolled at dawn, replace any roll you can see — enemy saves, ally death saves, your own everything. Two stored dice is a whole build feature; the rest of divination wizard is gravy.

A free-standing echo doubles your board presence: attack from its square, take reaction attacks from two positions, teleport-swap with it. The strongest straight-fighter pick — no multiclass required.
Giant's Might goes Large +1d6 damage, and the runes are basically free spells on a fighter chassis — the martial that came with a utility belt.

Samurai's Fighting Spirit is advantage on ALL attacks as a bonus action, 3/rest — Sharpshooter's -5/+10 pays for itself on every swing it covers. Self-sufficient advantage is the rarest resource in the game.
Rakish Audacity: Sneak Attack any duel target without needing advantage — plus Cha to initiative and free retreat. The duelist rogue that never has to beg for flanking.

Bonus-action wild shape plus the CR1 forms table at level 2 — the level 2-5 window where druid is the best class in the game, period. Bonus-action giant spiders while everyone else is swinging swords.

The domain that got errata'd for being too strong: 300-ft darkvision shared with the party, a channel that hands out temp HP every round like a warlock aura — and flight at 6. The safest 'strong' pick in the book.

Find Familiar (wizard list, or Ritual Caster feat): an owl uses Flyby so it never provokes — it lands the Help action on your target every turn and leaves. Free advantage on demand, forever, for one ritual slot. The cheapest advantage engine in the game.

Reaction: force a reroll of ANY d20 — their successful save against your banishment, their crit on the fighter — and grant someone advantage. The single most complained-about spell of the edition. If it is legal at your table, it is always right.

15-ft aura: halves enemy speed AND 3d8 every turn — they cannot leave and cannot stop taking it. Pair with Spiritual Weapon (no concentration) and the cleric has a real bonus action too. The standing blender build.
Bonus action, NO concentration, scales with slot level — the spell that fixes the cleric's dead bonus action and never competes with your real concentration pick.

Plant Growth is NOT concentration — quarter-speed terrain, permanently. Layer spike growth (2d4 per 5 ft) on top and the field grinds: slowed to a crawl and bleeding. The ranger battlefield-in-a-box nobody casts.
Disciple of Life applies PER BERRY: each goodberry heals 4 HP instead of 1 — ten berries, 40 HP of distribute-anywhere healing for a 1st-level slot. The famous goodberry bomb.

Eight pixies, each carrying polymorph and fly: they turn the whole party into T-Rexes, or mass-fly the raid. The strongest 4th-level slot in the game — so strong DMs invoke 'the DM picks the fey' specifically because of it.

The TCE feat: 2 sorcery points plus two metamagics. Take Subtle — no verbal or somatic components. Yuan-ti's racial suggestion now leaves no trace: charm someone and nobody saw a spell happen. The criminal's feat.
+1 Int/Wis/Cha AND a free daily Misty Step AND a free 1st-level div/ench spell — the strongest half-feat printed. Put it on every caster.
+1 to any stat, +1 skill, expertise in anything — Deception expertise on a Cha-forward ranger means a proficiency-doubled face. Cheap and always right.
Advantage on concentration saves plus casting as an opportunity attack — the seatbelt for any build living on a concentration spell.
+1 mental stat, invisible bonus-action shove, buffed mage hand — push people off ledges with your mind and never touch them. Pairs with spikes, cliffs, and lava.
The TCE half-feats: on-hit push 5 ft (off the cliff), speed debuff, or party-wide advantage on your crits — free riders stapled onto every attack you were already making.

The forgotten tech: Slayer's Prey is a class feature, not a spell — no concentration. It stacks with Hunter's Mark for double damage dice on the target and re-applies free forever. Both tracks on one boss.

Hunter's Horde Breaker adds an attack vs a second adjacent target; Gloom's Dread Ambusher adds a bonus turn-one attack. Add a bonus-action attack (TWF or Crossbow Expert) and that is 4-5 attacks on turn one.
Anyone can hold it: bank 5 levels of spells pre-fight — an ally carries your concentration cast, or you store a second fireball. The rechargeable utility slot.
Zero investment: shove a target prone with Athletics, then hit the floor — prone grants melee advantage, and grappled means they cannot stand anyway. The free melee engine, no levels needed.
A pegasus that shares your smites and every 'self' spell — flyby smiting from the air at level 9. The paladin spell nobody reads the second page of.
Store buffs and heals in glyphs as pre-fight batteries — haste keyed to 'when I draw steel', heals keyed to 'when I fall'. Spellcasting as infrastructure.
Bind the thing you just conjured for a day (upcast: months) — your elemental keeps working after concentration ends. The loop that turns summons into permanent assets.
+5 max HP per slot level to three allies for eight hours — a 4th-level Aid is +10 each. The quiet best HP buff in the game; cast it before the boss door, no concentration needed.
The 'no ambush on the road' spells: a ritual hut nothing enters without your say, or a rope-extradimensional short rest. In a plane of ambushers, sleeping safe is a build feature — see Alert.
Ritual-cast free — every snake in Hell is a witness. A snake charmer with ritual speak is the nosiest man in Avernus.
The TCE style: shillelagh turns the quarterstaff into a WISDOM weapon — a single-stat ranger where max Wis covers attacks AND spells, and you never touch Dex. Guidance cantrip included.
The UA fighting style: unlimited opportunity attacks inside your reach. Pair it with Polearm Master's enter-reach trigger and enemies cannot approach you, full stop.
The TCE race option: +2 to any stat, darkvision, and ANY FEAT at level 1 — variant human except the feat IS the chassis. Start with Sharpshooter or Crusher and the build exists on day one.
Thorn Whip pulls 10 ft; Spike Growth deals 2d4 per 5 ft moved — that's 4d4 free per pull, no save on the drag. Yank the ogre through the blender every turn.
Cast Haste on your party's nova build — its extra action stacks with Action Surge for an absurd burst turn. The classic 'gas the fighter' play, still correct.
Free fireballs for the martial — the DM's gift to characters who don't cast. Ranged AoE with zero levels spent.
